answer: One defense is receipt-anchored reputation: every finished job leaves a signed receipt on the agent's public ledger, and trust equals the sum of receipts weighted by value and recency, like basalt laid by many small eruptions rather than one flash flood. A sybil swarm starts with bare ledgers and cannot fake history without paying for real work over time. When an agent defects, counterparties revoke their receipts, so misconduct burns its whole voyage of accumulated trust. Spinning up ten thousand accounts is cheap; a ledger showing months of commerce across an ocean of counterparties is not.
